q: A proclamation is issued on the basis of material that is wholly irrelevant, the satisfaction being subjective. Which statement is correct?
options: The satisfaction is reviewable to the extent of examining whether relevant material existed
The satisfaction is wholly beyond review, being subjective in terms of the provision
The satisfaction is reviewable in full, the court substituting its own assessment
The satisfaction is reviewable only where the Governor did not submit a report
expl: Limited review examines the existence and relevance of material, not its sufficiency.
why: The second and third options represent the two extremes the courts have rejected in this area.
trapnote: Limited review sits between no review and full review. Both extremes are wrong.

q: Cabinet approval for a Proclamation is given orally at night and the Proclamation issues the next morning. Which statement is correct?
options: The Proclamation is valid, oral advice being sufficient where urgency exists
The Proclamation is valid, the writing requirement applying only to extensions
The Proclamation is defective, the advice requiring the Prime Minister's signature alone
The Proclamation is defective, written Cabinet advice being a condition precedent
expl: Written recommendation of the Cabinet is required before the Proclamation is issued.
why: The fourth option reaches the right conclusion by inventing a signature requirement, a wrong reason for a right result.
trapnote: The 1978 amendment requires Cabinet advice in writing, not the Prime Minister's advice alone.

q: Consider a claim that the financial emergency carries the same three-year outer limit as President's Rule. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: both are subject to the same three-year outer limit
The claim fails: the outer limit for the financial emergency is one year
The claim fails: the financial emergency has no such outer limit prescribed
The claim fails: the outer limit applies to the national Emergency instead
expl: Once approved, the financial emergency continues indefinitely until revoked.
why: Three options offer an outer limit of some kind, which makes the absence of any limit counter-intuitive.
trapnote: Only President's Rule carries a three-year cap. The other two have no equivalent outer limit.

q: A Governor recommends President's Rule after receiving letters withdrawing support, refusing a floor test. Which statement is correct?
options: The recommendation is conclusive, the Governor's satisfaction not being reviewable
The recommendation is open to challenge; the floor of the House is the proper forum
The recommendation is valid, letters being sufficient evidence of loss of majority
The recommendation is open to challenge only after the proclamation is approved
expl: Majority is tested in the House, not assessed from correspondence.
why: The fourth option adds a timing condition that does not exist and is attractive as a compromise position.
trapnote: Loss of majority is a question for the House. Correspondence is not a substitute for a vote.

q: Consider: 1-The national Emergency may be confined to a part of the territory. 2-President's Rule necessarily extends to the whole State. 3-The order suspending remedies may be confined to a part of the territory. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: National Emergency and remedy-suspension orders can be territorial; President Rule necessarily covers the whole State.
why: The second statement is the defect and is plausible because a State is the natural unit of that proclamation.
trapnote: Territorial limitation is available for the national Emergency and the suspension order.

q: An officer refuses to produce a detained person before a magistrate during a Proclamation of Emergency. Which statement is correct?
options: The refusal is lawful, the liberty guarantee standing suspended by the Proclamation
The refusal is lawful if a Presidential order suspending remedies has been made
The refusal is unlawful unless the Proclamation rests on external aggression
The refusal is unlawful, the liberty guarantee not being suspendable at all
expl: The liberty guarantee cannot be suspended, so the production requirement survives.
why: The third option is the strongest distractor because such an order can suspend remedies for other rights.
trapnote: The suspension order cannot reach these two articles, whatever else it covers.

q: A State government is dismissed, the Assembly is dissolved, and the proclamation is later held invalid. Which statement is correct?
options: The Court may declare the proclamation invalid but cannot revive the Assembly
The Court may restore the Ministry but cannot revive a dissolved Assembly
The Court may revive the Assembly and restore the Ministry
The Court's declaration operates prospectively and leaves the dissolution intact
expl: Revival and restoration were both expressly recognised as available remedies.
why: Three options offer partial remedies, which is persuasive because full restoration seems an extraordinary step.
trapnote: The remedy recognised is full: revival of the House and restoration of the Ministry.

q: Consider the suspension of remedies by Presidential order: 1-It suspends the right itself. 2-It suspends the right to move a court. 3-It must be laid before Parliament. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It suspends the remedy rather than the right, and must be laid before Parliament.
why: The distinction between suspending a right and suspending access to a court is the core of this provision.
trapnote: The right survives; the door to the court closes. That distinction decides most questions here.

q: A claim is made that during President's Rule the fundamental rights of residents of the State stand suspended. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails: President's Rule does not suspend any fundamental right
The claim succeeds: the six freedoms stand suspended in that State
The claim succeeds if the Union issues a direction to that effect
The claim fails: only the right to property stands suspended
expl: President's Rule transfers State functions; it does not touch fundamental rights.
why: The confusion between the two proclamations is the single most common error in the whole topic.
trapnote: Only the national Emergency affects rights. President's Rule concerns the State machinery.

q: A Proclamation rests on war; a detention is challenged; a State Bill is reserved; and a State government is dismissed without a vote. Which statement correctly characterises the four limbs?
options: Freedoms suspended automatically, liberty suspended, reservation invalid, dismissal conclusive
Freedoms intact, liberty enforceable, reservation valid, dismissal conclusive
Freedoms suspended automatically, liberty enforceable, reservation invalid, dismissal conclusive
Freedoms suspended automatically, liberty enforceable, reservation valid, dismissal challengeable
expl: War triggers automatic suspension of the freedoms; liberty survives; reservation is a normal power; dismissal without a vote is challengeable.
why: Each wrong option is correct on two or three limbs, so a candidate who stops early will choose one of them.
trapnote: Four limbs, four separate rules. Carry the analysis to the last limb before choosing.
